33	 * One item per signed document: an emergency department provider note, an admission history and

35	 * usually belong to one hospital encounter; the `encounter` entry in each item says which.

37	 * The narrative is the note text the clinician signed. The payload holds the structured parts of the
38	 * note as the hospital EHR stored them when the note was signed: the encounter context, diagnoses, the
39	 * home medication list, inpatient medications, allergies, vital signs, and copies of lab results the
40	 * author reviewed.
41	 *
42	 * Read these before mapping:
43	 *
44	 * - **Every document re-lists the home medications and allergies.** Each list is a snapshot taken when
45	 *   that document was signed, with that document's status for each drug. Five documents in one stay
46	 *   mean five copies of the same drugs. For the hospital's final word on outpatient medications, use the
47	 *   most recent `discharge_summary` of the encounter.
48	 * - **Lab results are copies.** Riverside does not publish lab results as items of their own. A result
49	 *   appears inside whichever documents reviewed it, so the same result can appear in several items. The
50	 *   `accession` plus test code identifies one result across documents.
51	 * - **Lab values are text**, exactly as the lab displayed them: `"182"`, `"7.21"`, `"<0.01"`.
52	 * - **Payload times are UTC** (`Z`). Riverside is in America/Chicago (UTC-6 standard, UTC-5 daylight
53	 *   time). The clinical date of an evening visit is the local date, which can be a day earlier than the
54	 *   UTC date. Times written in the narrative are local wall-clock times.
55	 * - **No allergy/intolerance distinction.** Everything on the hospital's allergy list is an `allergy`
56	 *   entry, including side effects such as cough.
57	 *
58	 * Envelope conventions: `effective` is the time the document is about (ED arrival for an ED note, time
59	 * of examination for an H&P, progress note or consult, inpatient admission time for a discharge
60	 * summary, with `effective_end` = discharge time). `author` is the signing clinician. A signed addendum
61	 * or correction is a new item that `supersedes` the original and restates the whole document.
62	 */
63	
64	/** One entry in a Riverside document payload. Discriminated by `type`. */
65	export type RiversideEntry =
66	  | Encounter
67	  | Diagnosis
68	  | History
69	  | Allergy
70	  | HomeMed
71	  | InpatientMed
72	  | Vitals
73	  | Result
74	  | Panel
75	  | FollowUp;

77	/**
78	 * The encounter and document context. Exactly one per item, conventionally under the key `enc`.
79	 */
80	export interface Encounter {
81	  type: 'encounter';
82	
83	  /**
84	   * Riverside encounter number. One number covers the whole hospital stay, from ED arrival to
85	   * discharge: the ED note, H&P, progress notes, consults and discharge summary of one stay share it.
86	   */
87	  encounter_id: string;
88	
89	  /**
90	   * Which kind of document this item is.
91	   * - 'ed_note': emergency department provider note.
92	   * - 'hp': admission history and physical, written by the admitting physician.
93	   * - 'progress_note': daily inpatient note.
94	   * - 'consult': note from a specialty service asked to see the patient.
95	   * - 'discharge_summary': written at discharge; covers the whole stay. Its home medication list is
96	   *   the discharge instructions.
97	   */
98	  document_kind: 'ed_note' | 'hp' | 'progress_note' | 'consult' | 'discharge_summary';
99	
100	  /**
101	   * Encounter class at the time the document was signed.
102	   * - 'emergency': the patient was in the ED and not yet admitted.
103	   * - 'inpatient': admitted (including step-down and ICU).
104	   * A stay that starts in the ED changes class from 'emergency' to 'inpatient' at admission; earlier
105	   * documents keep the class they were signed with.
106	   */
107	  class: 'emergency' | 'inpatient';
108	
109	  /** Clinical service of the author, free text as configured at Riverside, e.g. "Emergency Medicine", "Hospital Medicine", "Endocrinology". */
110	  service: string;
111	
112	  /** ED arrival time, UTC. Present on every document of a stay that began in the ED. */
113	  arrived?: string;
114	
115	  /** Inpatient admission order time, UTC. Absent while the patient is still in the ED. */
116	  admitted?: string;
117	
118	  /** Discharge time, UTC. Present only on discharge summaries. */
119	  discharged?: string;
120	
121	  /**
122	   * Where the patient went at the end of this phase of care.
123	   * - 'admitted': ED patient admitted to Riverside (ED notes only).
124	   * - 'home': discharged home without services.
125	   * - 'home_with_services': discharged home with home health.
126	   * - 'transferred': sent to another hospital.
127	   * - 'left_against_advice': left before the care team discharged them.
128	   * Absent on H&Ps, progress notes and consults.
129	   */
130	  disposition?: 'admitted' | 'home' | 'home_with_services' | 'transferred' | 'left_against_advice';
131	}

137	 */

143

153	   * SGLT2 inhibitor-associated euglycemic DKA from other DKA, which share ICD-10-CM E11.10). Code

196	   * - 'outside_records': another organization's records (e.g. a primary care summary).

204	 * "Allergies" and does not separate allergies from intolerances or side effects: a drug that once
205	 * caused a cough is listed the same way as one that caused anaphylaxis. Read `reaction` to tell them

209	  type: 'allergy';

247

250

262

453	 * Consumer views, version 2: the small shapes a patient-facing chart app reads.
454	 *
455	 * These are defined by the consumer, not by any source. A mapper turns one source's FOLIO record items
456	 * for one patient into these rows. The consumer merges rows from several sources itself, so a mapper

458	 * what the source records.
459	 *
460	 * Contract (see `Transform`): the mapper receives every item one source published for one patient,
461	 * in no particular order and including items that were later superseded or retracted, plus an
462	 * `asOf` date. It returns the rows that describe that source's record as it stood at the end of that
463	 * date.
464	 *
465	 * Conventions for every view:
466	 *
467	 * - **Scope in time.** An item is in scope when its envelope `recorded` time is on or before the end of
468	 *   the `asOf` day in America/Chicago. Ignore items recorded later. Apply the FOLIO correction rules to
469	 *   the items in scope: an item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` (same
470	 *   issuer) is not current; supersession is transitive. Use only current items, except where a view
471	 *   below says otherwise.

477	 *   means some time in 2016, never 2016-01-01. Never pad a year-only or month-only date.

479	 *   used to understand an entry but must not be the only basis for a row.
480	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and payload entry ids) it was built from, so the consumer
481	 *   can show the source text behind a fact. Cite at least the item whose entry gives the row's current
482	 *   state.
483	 * - **Sensitive entries are reported, never dropped.** Report every entry the source holds, including
484	 *   ones it marks restricted, confidential or sensitive. Mark such rows with `sensitivity` (see
485	 *   `Sensitivity`). Whether a sensitive fact is shown or shared is decided later, by the patient, at
486	 *   disclosure time; it is never decided by a mapper.
487	 * - **Determinism.** Same input, same output: no clock, randomness, network or file access.

- Losartan 50 mg tablet, 1 tablet by mouth daily: <ref id="med_losartan">held; PCP to decide on restarting after a repeat BMP</ref>.
